the 2015 scheme said once in 3 years — now cards are issued every two years (PMF Environment 06 p.125; PIB factsheet Aug 2025)
The Soil Health Card Scheme (2015) said each farm would get a card once in every 3 years, the AEE 2016 key (now issued every two years). 2, 4 and 5 years were not the scheme's stated interval.

s: What are the cards that have been issued to the tenant farmers through the Department of Agriculture in AP to facilitate the availability of institutional credit, crop insurance, farm implements and input subsidy?
src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2019
x:
COC / Loan Eligibility Cards — now Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRCs) under the AP Crop Cultivators Rights Act 2019; 9,13,283 issued by 3 Jan 2025 (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.56)
AP issued Certificates of Cultivation (COC) cards, with Loan Eligibility Cards, so tenant farmers could get institutional credit, insurance and input subsidy (now Crop Cultivator Rights Cards under the 2019 Act). Soil Health Cards only give nutrient advice.

s: The descending order of the following States from the point of view of wheat production in the country is :
x:
Printed key: Haryana, Rajasthan, Bihar, MP – never true. Strictly: Haryana > MP > Rajasthan > Bihar in 2009-10 and 2010-11 (option a); in 2007-08 and 2008-09 Haryana > Rajasthan > MP > Bihar (option b) (RBI Handbook Table 49).
wheat order — since 2011-12 MP has overtaken Haryana (2012-13: MP 13.1 MT, Haryana 11.1 MT) and is now India's 2nd wheat State (RBI Handbook Table 49)
RBI state data: Haryana 10.5 and 11.6 MT, MP 8.4 and 7.6, Rajasthan 7.5 and 7.2, Bihar 4.6 and 4.1 MT in 2009-10 and 2010-11 – order Haryana, MP, Rajasthan, Bihar. Bihar never exceeded MP, so the printed key (d) is wrong; in 2007-08 and 2008-09 Rajasthan was ahead of MP.

s: The State is the largest producer of rice in India.
x:
rice leader — West Bengal (to 2021-22) → Telangana (2023-24) → now Uttar Pradesh (2024-25) (app notes 3:50 sub 4)
In 2017-19 West Bengal was the largest rice producer.

s: Total food grains production (including pulses) in the country is now
x:
the stem's "now" is 1983-84 — now a record 357.73 MT in 2024-25 and 376.56 MT in 2025-26 (2nd AE) (app notes 3:50 sub 2)
Around 1983-84 India's foodgrain output stood at about 130-150 MT (about 133 MT in 1981-82, about 152 MT in 1983-84); 10-20, 80-90 and 200-240 MT are far off.
flag: Stem 'now' = 1983-84; current output is about 357.73 MT (2024-25), so the key is outdated. | 200-240 MT was reached only around 2000-2010; in 1983-84 it was about 130-150 MT.

s: According to the latest estimates of the Ministry of Agriculture, during 2011-12 the foodgrains production in the country is estimated to be
x:
2011-12 "latest estimate" — final 2011-12 output 259.29 MT; now 357.73 MT in 2024-25 (app notes 3:50 sub 2)
The Ministry of Agriculture's third advance estimates (May 2012) put 2011-12 foodgrains at 252.56 MT, a record then (final 259.29 MT).

s: India is the largest producer of which agricultural products?
x:
rice — India overtook China in 2025-26 (150.18 vs 145.28 MT, Jan 2026), so rice is now also a 1st-rank crop, but option (a) still fails on wheat and cotton (app notes 3:50 sub 3)
India is the world's largest producer of milk, pulses and spices; it is 2nd in rice (until 2025), wheat, sugarcane and cotton, and not 1st in tea or coffee.

s: What is the extent of land and the number of instalments through which the farmers are able to get ₹ 6000/- per annum under Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana?
src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
x:
2-hectare limit — from June 2019 PM-KISAN covers all landholding farmer families irrespective of size (still ₹6,000 in 3 instalments) (general knowledge, not checked)
At its launch PM-KISAN gave ₹6,000 a year in three instalments to small and marginal families holding up to 2 hectares.
flag: Outdated: since June 2019 all landholding families are eligible regardless of size.

the old figure was 2.76 crore property cards — now 3.06 crore (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.153, January 2026)
SVAMITVA had prepared 3.06 crore property cards in 1.86 lakh villages by January 2026 (earlier figure 2.76 crore).

s: To how many crore poor families at present, the Public Distribution System (PDS) provides subsidised food grains in India?
x: In 2012 TPDS gave subsidised grain to about 6.52 crore BPL families (including 2.43 crore AAY), the nearest option being 6.5 crore.
flag: 'At present' figure is dated (c. 2012); NFSA now counts persons (~81 crore), not families.

the FAO count has been revised and has fallen — now 224.3 million undernourished in 2019-21 (SOFI 2022, theweek.in 7 Jul 2022); 12.0% of the population as per SOFI 2025 (app notes 3:59 sub 9)
FAO's estimate of that time put India's undernourished at about 245 million (revised series: 247.8 million in 2004-06) (now 224.3 million in 2019-21, SOFI 2022).

s: Which of the following states is the largest producer of flowers in India?

Around 2004 Karnataka (floriculture around Bengaluru) was given as the largest flower producer. (now Tamil Nadu leads with about 21%, Karnataka 16%)
flag: Outdated key: Tamil Nadu is now the largest flower producer (~21%), Karnataka 16%. | Per the old key Karnataka led; Tamil Nadu leads today (~21%).

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
x:
India was 3rd (after China and the USA) when older keys were set — now 2nd in world egg production (DAHD BAHS 2024)
India is now the 2nd largest egg producer in the world after China (142.77 billion eggs, 2023-24); older books and keys gave 3rd (after China and the USA).
flag: Older keys gave 'Third'; key 'Second' matches current DAHD data. Linked note is about fisheries, not eggs. | India was 3rd earlier (after China, USA); now 2nd.

s: On which of the following commodities is the dual-pricing policy enforced in India?
x: Dual pricing (levy sugar at a fixed price plus free-sale sugar) applied to sugar; cement and steel were decontrolled earlier and petrol never had it.
flag: Levy sugar obligation ended in 2013; cement too had dual pricing (1982-89). Linked note is unrelated. | Cement had dual pricing only until decontrol (1982-89).

s: Small enterprises refer to those units which have got gross fixed capital of

the limits were raised again from 1 April 2025 (Budget 2025-26) — now the latest classification is 2025 (app notes 3:62)
The latest MSME classification at the 2021 exam was the 2020 composite investment-plus-turnover one (now revised again, from 1 April 2025).

o: Number of workers in the Enterprise
Investment in the plant and machinery and equipment of the Enterprise
Investment in plant and machinery and equipment as well as annual turnover of the Enterprise

flag: | Investment alone was the basis until 2020; now turnover is added.

s: What is the current investment limit in Small Scale Industry?
x: In 2004 the SSI investment limit was Rs 1 crore (100 lakh), set in 1999.
flag: Outdated: 'current' now means MSMED 2020 limits (small: investment up to Rs 10 cr, later 25 cr). | Rs 20 lakh was the 1980 limit.; Rs 60 lakh was the 1991 limit.

s: Which of the following partly defines the micro-enterprise in India?
o: Investment in Plant and Machinery or equipment not
Annual turnover not more than Rs. 15 crore
Investment in Plant and Machinery not more than Rs
Annual turnover of more than Rs. 5 crore
Annual turnover not more than Rs. 5 crore
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Annual turnover not more than Rs. 5 crore); it is added as option 5.
micro turnover ceiling Rs 5 crore (2020) — now Rs 10 crore from 1 April 2025 (app notes 3:62)
Under the 2020 criteria a micro enterprise has investment up to Rs 1 crore and turnover up to Rs 5 crore (now Rs 2.5 crore / Rs 10 crore). The printed 'turnover not more than Rs 15 crore' was never a limit, the investment options are cut off in the source, and 'more than Rs 5 crore' is wrong.

s: Investment in Plant and Machinery in a small scale manufacturing unit should be :
o: Above Rs. 10 lakh but not more than Rs. 25 lakh
Above Rs. 25 lakhs but not more than Rs. 5 crore
Above Rs. 5 crore but not more than Rs.10 crore
x:
2006 limit Rs 25 lakh-5 crore — now small = investment up to Rs 25 crore and turnover up to Rs 100 crore (from 1 April 2025) (app notes 3:62)
Under the MSMED Act 2006 a small manufacturing unit invested above Rs 25 lakh and up to Rs 5 crore in plant and machinery (now up to Rs 25 crore with turnover up to Rs 100 crore).

x: Since 1991, India's policy has been to encourage foreign multinationals with automatic FDI approval, foreign brand names and repatriation.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

s:

Indian Railways set targets of 100% electrification by 2023 and a net-zero carbon network by 2030, so both statements are correct (electrification reached about 99% of broad gauge by 2025).

s: Union Minister for Railways and Commerce Piyush Goyal has announced that the entire network of railways in the country will run on electricity by ____.
src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
